title: Parity of a Shifted Reciprocal Function h(t) = 1 / (t - 1)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the function h(t) = 1 / (t - 1) is even, odd, or neither, and justify your answer.

steps.title: Inspect the Domain and Evaluate h(-t)
steps.explanation: First observe that the domain t != 1 is not symmetric about 0 (since t = -1 is in the domain while t = 1 is not). Furthermore, substituting -t gives h(-t) = -1 / (t + 1).
steps.why: A shifted vertical asymptote at t = 1 breaks both y-axis and origin symmetry.

steps.title: Compare h(-t) with h(t) and -h(t)
steps.explanation: Evaluating at t = 2 gives h(2) = 1, whereas at t = -2 we get h(-2) = -1/3, which equals neither h(2) nor -h(2).
steps.why: If a function is even or odd, |h(-t)| must equal |h(t)| for all t in the domain.

steps.title: Conclude Function Parity
steps.explanation: Because neither symmetry condition holds, h(t) = 1 / (t - 1) is neither even nor odd.
steps.why: Horizontal translation of 1/t by 1 unit to the right destroys its origin symmetry.
